title: Noor and the Ember
premise: August Eriksen has survived fifteen years in the magic-outlawed city of Vhalen by keeping his beast-speaking gift small and secret—until a date with the archivist Sefa turns up their names in a century-old prophecy book that shouldn't exist. Hunted by the Ash Wardens and shadowed by Noor, a fire-fox spirit bound to the prophecy's 'ember,' August learns the gift he's hidden is the last living thread of an ancient war the city was built to bury. To save Sefa from the fate the book assigns them, August must embrace the forbidden magic fully, unbind Noor at the cost of his own power, and burn the prophecy itself—choosing an unwritten future over survival on anyone else's terms.
about_author: R. M. Montrose is the pen name of a former wildlife rehabilitator who spent a decade listening to animals no one else could reach before turning to fiction. They write quiet, fierce fantasies about outsiders who talk to things that cannot answer back.

chapters.title: Charms for Small Coin
chapters.summary: August's POV. In the market of Vhalen, August sells harmless charms while quietly bargaining with rats and pigeons to keep the streets safe, hiding his gift behind mundane tricks. A near-discovery by an Ash Warden leaves him shaken but intact. The beat: weary competence masking loneliness—he has survived by being small.

chapters.title: The Archivist's Date
chapters.summary: August's POV. August meets Sefa, a warm, sharp-tongued archivist he's been courting for months, in the restricted stacks where she works. She shows him a sealed prophecy book as a flirtation; when it opens, both their names glow on a page dated tomorrow. The beat: wonder curdling into dread—the past has been waiting for them.

chapters.title: What the Fox Carried
chapters.summary: August's POV. Fleeing the archive as Wardens seal the district, August is found by Noor, a fire-fox spirit who speaks in embers and claims August summoned her by reading the book aloud. She marks him with a brand only he can see. The beat: terror and reluctant awe—a secret shared is a self transformed.

chapters.title: The War Beneath the Cobblestones
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Sefa deciphers the prophecy: fifteen years ago the Wardens didn't end the mage war—they buried its survivors beneath the city, and the 'ember' is the last spark that can wake them. She realizes her own name appears as the sacrifice that keeps them sleeping. The beat: guilt sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: Ash Wardens at the Door
chapters.summary: August's POV. The Wardens raid August's shop; his mentor Odile covers his escape and is taken. Noor reveals the brand will let the Wardens track him anywhere. August must choose between running alone or pulling Sefa deeper into danger. The beat: the price of survival becomes someone else's blood.

chapters.title: Bargains with Rats
chapters.summary: August's POV. Hiding in the undercity, August uses his gift openly for the first time, rallying the beasts of Vhalen's sewers into a ragged intelligence network. He finds Odile alive in a Warden cell and learns the Wardens want the ember not destroyed but claimed. The beat: found family forming among the overlooked.

chapters.title: The Page That Writes Back
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Sefa discovers the prophecy book is still writing—new ink appears describing tonight's choices before they make them. Every attempt to change the ending only feeds it. She hides this from August, planning to surrender herself instead. The beat: love expressed as secrecy, the first fracture between them.

chapters.title: Noor's True Name
chapters.summary: August's POV. Noor confesses she is not a messenger but the war's final casualty—a mage burned into fox-shape, kept alive as bait so the buried survivors would have a reason to rise. The Wardens' trap springs: Odile, Sefa, and August are all drawn to the same crypt. The beat: betrayal reframed as grief.

chapters.title: The Ember Rises
chapters.summary: Alternating POV, climax. In the crypt, the buried mages wake as the Wardens attempt to seize the ember through Noor. August speaks every beast-name he knows, turning the city's animals against both armies, while Sefa tears the final page from the book and refuses the sacrifice written for her. The beat: defiance—no one dies on schedule.

chapters.title: An Unwritten Morning
chapters.summary: August's POV, resolution. August gives his gift to Noor, unbinding her into her true form and leaving himself ordinary; the prophecy burns to ash, and the freed mages negotiate exile rather than war. Sefa stays, choosing him without a book's permission. The beat: bittersweet peace—survival redefined as a future no one predicted.
